Though I use Windows XP, my computer is old and my processor (Sempron) is not what is required to run the "KODAK Share Button" app to transfer videos from the Kodak Playful, Model Ze2 to my computer. That's too bad. But anyway, be sure to check the specs before buying so this won't happen to you. I downloaded the program anyway but it wouldn't run. So, I've tried just about everything I know to do and nothing seems to work. An old "FinePixViewer" program keeps popping up every time I try to download a video, but it takes a very long time for it to finally work. I guess technology is trying to force me to buy a newer/faster computer because so many gadgets won't work on poor ole' Bessie anymore despite her having 34 GB left of memory and 4GB of ram.

The camera itself is fun to play with and I like the 1970's film mode, but it would be better if the theme to "Shaft" was being quietly played in the background while using that particular mode. The access doors are very difficult to open and you will probably lose some fingernails until you get it figured out. The Kodak website is not very good.....I never could find a place where I could ask a question directly to technical support. And the web addresses provided in the manual take you to the same web page regardless of the the specifics written into the web address like: [...]. They all take you to the same place and you have to hunt and peck where you want to go and what you're looking for. And they have no Ze2 demos to watch - go figure. And though Windows XP is listed in a drop menu, when I click on it absolutely nothing happens. So much for Windows XP help.

I'm giving it 3 stars because the doors are a pain, and the website is inadequate. But since I don't own a computer that will allow the Kodak program to work I can't fairly judge the quality of the videos. When I can get FinePixView to play them they look alright. I have yet to connect the Kodak Playful directly to my HDTV to see how the HD (720) quality and sound are, and I will do that and report back. I am very interested especially in the sound quality since I'm a musician/music teacher and like to record my students playing.

Our AV department bought a BDP-300 so we could release our HD video content on Blu-ray. We bought the expensive Blu-ray burner for the computer, we bought the expensive authoring software, we bought a bunch of expensive BD-R and BD-RW recordable disks and we bought the expensive Sony BDP-300 player, with an eye toward buying a bunch more for our conference rooms if the system worked. It didn't.

We found that the BDP-300 will not play back BD-R or BD-RW discs. Though it might have been possible to be upgraded via a firmware update (like its REALLY expensive big brother can be firmware upgraded) it most likely never will. Thanks a lot, Sony. Way to make an integrated system. No wonder Blu-ray has been so slow to catch on. Thus we as a very large company cannot commit to Blu-ray because we can't play the recorded Blu-ray disks back on even a $400 player. Sigh.

Secondly, if you connect to a digital display that only has DVI-in via an HDMI/DVI adapter or an HDMI/DVI cable adapter, the player doesn't work. I suspect the problem is connected to copy protection schemes built into the multiple HDMI standards.

So, if you have an older HD display that only has DVI-in, forget this "reasonably priced" Blu-ray player. You'll most likely need to use the analog YRB (component) outputs, which is an inferior signal to the digital HDMI output. I did a component/HDMI comparison for my wife and she definitely picked the HDMI as the superior output picture.

There is a workaround that allows the HDMI/DVI to work, but it's a pain: First, connect both the HDMI and component cables to their respective inputs on the display. Now, before powering the player on, manually disconnect the HDMI cable from the back of the player while leaving the component cables connected to the display. Then power up the player and switch the display to the analog "component" input. You can now see the menus and the Blu-ray disk will be able to be played. After you get the movie running, manually plug the HDMI/DVI cable into the back of the player and switch the display to the digital DVI input. The Blu-ray disk now works and allows the menus and other overlaid controls to function normally. As different HDMI copy protection schemes get adopted this trick might fail.

If you have HDMI-in on your display, the player might work, but no guarantees. Bear in mind that the HDMI standard is constantly changing. I think they're up to at least HDMI 1.3 so far, and counting. And a totally new plug protocol is on its way for computer monitors, too, called DisplayPort, which might make it to TV sets, but who knows?

After this little problem was overcome, I finally got to see the picture. It was very nice, especially after I got to see it via my HDMI-DVI workaround. Definitely better than the analog component feed.

The overlaid menus allow you to access the menu anytime, without leaving the movie. Pretty cool. The menus are also more animated and better integrated.

Audio quality is fabulous. Both Dolby and DTS sound great because with all the storage capacity on the disk, the signals don't have to be compressed as much as they are for a standard DVD.

If you want the very, very best audio, though, you can select "uncompressed" and route the RCA audio outputs directly into your amp's dedicated preamp inputs. This takes the Dolby and DTS compression systems out of the picture altogether. So you are hearing multiple uncompressed audio tracks sent directly to your amp.

The worst part of the Blu-ray player is the time it takes to "boot" up. It's really a dedicated computer running an operating system. Java, at least, and maybe more. Thus it takes a full two minutes to fire up. You press the power button and nothing happens. After about ten seconds, you get a display that says "power on." After about 90 seconds, the machine is finally ready to play your disk. Give it a lot of time to fire up, especially the very first time you plug it in. After the initial plug-in/power-on sequence, the manual says it will be subsequently faster. But not by much. And the system can "crash," requiring you to turn it off and reboot. It happened several times to me as I moved too quickly between menu selections.

Overall, this player can put out a great picture, eventually, and after learning a bunch of quirks. I don't think it's ready for prime time, though. For the price it should be much better: faster boot up and with the ability to play back recorded Blu-ray disks.

Buy the BDP-300 knowing you will be replacing it for some reason in a year or two.

UPDATE:

I rented Universal's Hellboy II on Blu-ray tonight.

It crashed the player. Think "Blue Screen of Death" but without the blue screen and a longer boot sequence. I repeated the process six times.

I was about to flame this inop player when here on Amazon it was suggested to update to Firmware 4.20.

I went to Sony's site and found even newer 4.30 firmware. You download the exe and click on it to uncompress it. This creates an ISO disk image. You burn this to a new CD as an image (very important--an IMAGE, not a data disk.) Turn on the player and stick the CD in. It took 13 minutes for the update to install. When it's done it says "DL OK" on the player.

Player works like it's supposed to. It will play BD-R, too. In fact, it can even play a weird hybrid I can make with Sony Vegas editing software where I can burn a Blu-ray disk image to a standard DVD and play it as a
Blu-ray.

Close call: I was about to give up on Blu-ray.

I am reviewing the ‘TruSound TruWireless Noise Cancelling Earbuds | True Wireless Earbuds with Charging Case for Buds and Phone | Comfortable, Secure Fit | Immersive Stereo Sound, Deep Bass | Easy Touch Control Operation’.
Based on my experience thus far I would like to share my thoughts.

Pros:
1- The sound is decent but compared to other Wireless Earbuds that I have tried, these are pretty average.
2- The case is rechargeable via the included 18650 battery. This allows you to have extra 18650 batteries on hand which is an interesting feature.
3- It comes with extra ear tips.
4- It comes with a mini USB cable and even a USB type A to Mini USB adapter.
5- Aesthetically the earbuds look nice, feel comfortable and don’t protrude much when wearing them.
6- They stay in place quite well and do not randomly fall out.
7- Earbuds are held in place magnetically when in the case charging.
8- They pair up real fast and very easy. I have had no issues at all with pairing.

Cons:
1- I ordered these based on the description stating “active noise reduction is also a standout feature of TruSound ear buds, ensuring a distraction-free audio experience”. I took this as they had ANC or Active Noise Control. This is not the case. These “isolate” the outside sounds via the ear tip inserted into the ear canal. If you get the right tip fit, they do “isolate” the outside sounds but just not as expected.
2- No USB type C. In my opinion all new devices should have USB C charging.
3- The case is a bit bulky due to the fact that it uses the 18650 battery.
4- The case is plastic and uses two plastic tabs to snap the lid closed. The design makes it really hard to open the case once it’s snapped shut. I am worried that I will break the plastic tabs at which point I would need to use a rubber band to keep the lid closed.
5- The Stand-By time is not the greatest. I fully charged the 18650 battery with my own charger when I first got the Earbuds. I used the Earbuds briefly while initially testing them and when I went back a couple of weeks later to try them again, the battery was already dead. I have other earbuds that have this same issue. I should be able to fully charge my earbuds, keep them in my backpack for a few weeks and have them ready to go when I want to use them.
6- No IPX rating? Pretty much all of the newer Earbuds these days have some kind of waterproof rating. It’s not advertised so I am not really sure if they are.
7- No Bluetooth 5.0? These have Bluetooth 4.2+EDR which isn’t bad, but there are sync issues when watching YouTube, Netflix ect. It’s not bad, but it’s noticeable and I could not use these to watch videos for too long.

Overall these TruSound Earbuds are average, and I feel that compared to the flooded market of True Wireless Earbuds these are a bit overpriced. With that said, I do like these but, I do feel there could be some improvements made that would ultimately increase the value.

This case was recommended in several build guides, and seemed to be highly rated on Amazon, but I must say I'm quite disappointed.

Pros:
(1) It does the job. It's roomy -- in fact, it's really big. There's room for a really big graphics card without taking out any drive cages.
(2) Comes with four quiet fans (2 intakes in front, one large intake on the side, one exhaust on the back), and room to add more on the top.
(3) Having a couple of usb3 ports and audio/mike ports in the front is very convenient. Having the power supply at the bottom (in the back) also worked well for me.
(4) All the bits come apart and back together without too much trouble.

Cons:
(1) I had a lot of trouble getting my EVGA power supply to install, because the screw holes didn't line up nicely. Finally managed it by using a combination of power and adapting to what the case gave me.
(2) The 5.25 drive bays go in the conventional way, with the backs near the mobo for easy connections. But the 2.5/3.5 drive bays go in sideways, which might seem convenient at first, but now you have their connectors on the other side of the box -- so you're threading your power and sata cables around, and creating a bulge of cables etc. And that extra wiring room that the case promises? It doesn't extend all the way to the front, apparently the artists overcame the engineers (or they fought and the users lost). This arrangement also means that it's harder to share your sata power cables, depending on what you're trying to do with your setup.
(3) As others have pointed out, those nice intake fans aren't standard, they would be hard to replace individually. I'd have to replace all of them with standard case fans, I think.

This is a workable, but not outstanding way to record phone calls. It only works with a corded phone. You plug the handset cord into the recorder dock, then plug the dock into the phone. It runs on either 2 AAA batteries or via a 5v adapter that plugs into the dock. The adapter is NOT included.

While it’s simple and easy to install, it’s not so simple to actually use. The screen is small and hard to read, and the buttons are tiny. Navigating (or even seeing) the on screen menus is tough.

You can pick from different recording options including recording speed (long play, regular and high quality), auto record or manual record. Some of the options are easy to select, such as record speed. Others, such as the timer function (e.g., setting it to record at a specific time) are cumbersome to set up.

The voice quality when recording on the dock in HQ mode is decent. Nothing spectacular, but workable. The device will store 2 hours on HQ mode, 5.5 hours in SP mode and 14 hours in LP mode. You can organize files into folders, delete files and protect files from the device itself without having to connect to a PC.

You can also use this as a regular digital recorder by detaching it from the dock. It has an internal mic that has limited pickup capabilities. It’s very unimpressive when used as a regular digital recorder – there are far better choices out there.

Playback can be via the device itself, with pause, FF and reverse functionality. You can also transfer the file to a PC using the USB connector on the dock. It includes software that must be used to transfer files. That’s the weakest part of the package by far – the software looks and works like it was programmed 20 years ago. It works, but it’s not at all intuitive or capable compared with even the most basic audio management program currently available.

I got this on an auction site for about $17 and, for that price, it’s OK. I only use it to record calls in manual mode, and play back the recording using the device so I don’t have to deal with the PC interface. For me that makes it worth the cost. However, if you have more demanding needs or want to transfer and work with files on a PC, give this a pass. There are too many limitations and problems to make it a worthwhile tool.

The specifications imply that this tablet is designed to accept a wireless sim card if the user decides to add an additional wireless telephone line. Most people purchase this wireless keyboard to use at home with their TV or other media setup. I actually purchased it to use at work as a more ergonomic option. No, this is not billed as an ergonomic keyboard, but the main issue I was having was reaching for the mouse, so I wanted something with a built-in trackpad. Surprisingly, there are VERY FEW options available, particularly within a reasonable price range (<50) and offered by a name brand company.

Prior to purchasing this keyboard, I tried another which featured the trackpad front and center ([[ASIN:B004KN7PZG Gear Head USB Smart Touch II Touchpad Keyboard]]). Unfortunately, that product was way too glitchy, and the size was not ideal. I thought that the center trackpad would work well given that I'm used to using one on my laptop at home (a [[ASIN:B00IPQXZ62 Dell XPS Convertible 2 in 1]], which has a near-ideal keyboard), but that did not seem to be the case. When I began looking for keyboards with a built-in trackpad on the side, this one by Microsoft seemed to be the only viable option, although I wasn't looking for wireless.

I did like that that the keyboard is Microsoft, and I like the clean look and design. Compared to the prior keyboard that I tried, this one definitely has a more comfortable feel. Although it is small, there is adequate spacing around the keys, something the prior keyboard lacked. There is no number pad--the trackpad replaces this--but as I never used this anyway, this is no loss for me. All of the keys are a nice size, including the shift keys (these are sometimes skimped upon). Unfortunately, there is no "End" key--I knew that upon purchasing, but I still miss it. What I did NOT realize is that in order to access the Function keys, you actually have to HOLD DOWN the "FN" button. This is a bit of a pain for me, as I use Refresh (F5) constantly, so this is now a 2-handed operation. This keyboard is also missing any kind of indicator for CAPS LOCK.

The trackpad is okay. I still have my mouse plugged in, and unfortunately, I find myself using it too often, as the trackpad is not completely reliable. It does accept multi-finger scrolling gestures, which is nice, and it does pretty well with simple up-down navigation; however, I have found that side-to-side is much more uneven. I do like that there is a left-hand click button on the right side of the keyboard, and I have made use of this at times. But I've also found that sometimes my palm randoming activates the trackpad when I am typing, causing the cursor to flip to a new spot on screen, which is annoying. So, at best, this has been just average.

This keyboard includes other features that I don't use--e.g., a volume control, a separate mute button (are both necessary?), home and other "hot" keys, etc. I'm assuming that these extras would be more beneficial to someone using the keyboard in a home media setting. For my needs, this keyboard has been okay. The layout is decent, although it could have been much, much better with a few minor changes. Depending on how you plan to use it, I would recommend it with reservations.

My first thought when I initially saw the Motorola Sphere 2-in-1Bluetooth Speaker with Over-Ear Headphones was, wow. It is extremely attractive and would definitely appeal to the young folks. Ironically, our house is full of loud, music playing teenagers who have very clear ideas about what sounds good and which products they prefer to use. They like speakers and headphones that offer clear sound quality with bass. We have a Bose Soundlink speaker, and VModa or Sennheiser earphones. So unfortunately when I reviewed these, I was comparing them with others that I have used. While this product might look good (definitely a 5), it needs to sound good. And this is where I am disappointed – in the sound quality.
In a nutshell:

Attractiveness – The Motorola Sphere is attractive. It is black and looks like a head with headphones.The system looks nice on a bookshelf, desk or dresser in a dorm room, bedroom, etc.. I do love the look.

Set up – The directions for setting up the device are easy to follow. Once you pair the headphones and the sphere (separately) to your phone (via Bluetooth), it is pretty easy to use. There is sometimes a lag when you disconnect or switch between the sphere and the headphones. You might have to press the button on the headphones to make the sound switch between the two devices.

Headphones – They are adjustable and the sound quality is good via the headphones.

Sound Quality – The sound quality is not good thru the speaker. I’d give it 2.5 at the most. To me the frequency response seemed a little high, which is why the sound thru the speaker is hollow or missing something, no matter the genre (i.e., classic, jazz, rap, rock) played. But a plus is that the quality of the sound thru the headphones is better, it is more balanced and therefore rates 3.5-4 (although the bass is still not heavy).

In conclusion, while I love the look and concept (2 in 1 – speaker and headphones) of the Motorola, I wouldn’t recommend it. I would instead suggest investing a little more money and getting a better more quality speaker.

I used to be a big Ultimate Ears guy from the aughts before they were bought by Logitech who killed their best product lines and replaced it with stuff like... THIS. The tiresome photos of impossibly gleeful adult-babies listening to music underwater and having the times of their lives thanks to this f——g speaker really gets cloying when it’s printed on literally everything except the device itself. Of course I don’t use any of the EQ tomfoolery and let it play as close to how the music was engineered to play and its just dandy. Okay then, good sound: check.

Ugh. Sorry, had a bit of a rant there.

I ordered the 'Malektronic Interstellar Premium Wireless Noise Cancelling Over-Ear Headphones' for review and would like to share my thoughts.

So I am no audiophile, but I do love a good quality headphone that is built well and sound good. Sounding good or even great is really subjective depending on personal preference. For the going retail price of these Malektronic Interstellar Premium Wireless Noise Cancelling Over-Ear Headphones, I really expected much more than what I personally find these to be. I'll break my experience and thoughts into a few main points that stood out to me.

Comfort - These are comfortable but they don't fit as snug as I would have liked. I have a small head for a 54yro male, and even on the smallest adjustment setting, they just don't hug my ears like I would have hoped for such an expensive set of headphones.

Noise Cancelling - yea this is a big one for me right hear (see what I did there). I am not at all impressed with the Noise Cancelling in these headphones for the price. I mean it's OK, but I have ANC wireless earbuds that do a much better job for about the same price. There are only two settings. ANC On and ANC Off. For me, It's really hard to tell whether I've turned it on or off. There is no indicator like others I have that would either beep or greet you with some kind of prompt letting you know which mode you are in (there are voice prompts when you turn them on or off so why not anything for ANC modes). In fact the only way I can truly tell that it's on or off, is to pause the song and push the ANC button at which point it's pretty clear. However, and with that said, I do notice that when it's on, the music almost sounds more heavy on the Bass. It's almost like the Bass is supposed to give that "ANC" feel. Remember, I am no audiophile but this is just my observation.

Sound - Now I can say this, and that is that these do sound good until you get close to max volume. At which point they just don't hold up to the volume. Not that they get really loud but if you have the ANC on and you are listening to a heavy Bass song, they tend to bottom out just a tad. It's not bad but again for this price point, I would have expected better. The highs are nice but even better when ANC is off. Mids are there and probably sound good in either mode really. Another thing I noticed is that if you take these off while the music is still playing at full volume, they sound like they are rattling and sound a bit distorted. However when you put them back on, there is no distortion like I noticed with them off. That was kind of strange.

Micro USB charging - I always have to point this out. It's 2020 companies and USB C should be the standard any more in my opinion. Just saying.

Build Quality - They aren't the worst I have seen or tried but at this price point they are not the best either. They are pretty much plastic although fairly solid.

Buttons - The buttons are hidden/covered near the edge of the ear pads and they took me a while to figure out where they are, but after using them for a while, I actually like the fact that they look to be buttonless.

Looks/design - These really do look nice both on and off. They don't look cheap which is nice, as I have some others that just look ugly and I refuse to wear haha. The design is well thought out and I do love how they fold flat and compact into the very nice hard case.

So with all that said, I do like these headphones. They sound pretty good. The ANC is meh but they are comfortable besides not fitting as snug as I would prefer. Build quality is decent and I do love they way they fold up and store nicely into the included hard case. Thank you for including this Maletronics! Micro USB charging is a bummer but they also can be used wired with the included cable if you forget to get them charged up. Battery life is not bad. 30hrs might be pushing it if you like to listen to them loud and are always using the ANC. I have yet to test that fully as the longest I generally go is maybe an hour at a time. So for me the battery life is fine.

Overall, I really want to love these, and I actually do like them a lot, but I am just not that "Wowed" at this price point. I have other brands at or around this price point that I like better. Now maybe I got a dud pair and that very well could be, but I don't dislike them. They are nice and I plan to keep them around as a back-up pair. I hope that this was helpful.

The disadvantage is that the sound quality is just not going to be as good as headphones that cover your ears. That is especially true for this pair of headphones.

I have a Dell laptop that has served me well and I also have an older Dell workstation that has been great. I had high hoped for this tower system, and unfortunately it doesn’t quite meet expectations. If you are looking for an affordable gaming system, this one will work on the lower end.

I’ll start with the positives.

It comes with a 7th-generation core i7 processor and it is definitely fast. It is not one of the low power consumption processors, so when you look at the CPU in the device manager you see 8 of them reported - this is a good thing.

Everything is integrated with this system and there are plenty of ports. You don’t need a separate graphics card (though you can add one - more on that in a minute), sound is built in, Bluetooth is built in too and it even has integrated wireless networking.

This is a very attractive system too, and it’s quiet. If you don’t like a noisy system\, this one has you covered.

It comes with 1TB storage. It’s disk-based so it’s slower than an SSD but with that amount of space you have more than enough space for most uses.

And, it’s affordable. It will not break the bank if you already have a monitor and keyboard/mouse combo.

And now for the bad news.

I am not the least bit impressed with the graphics card. With modern games the more graphics memory you have the better, and having only 2GB video RAM is not enough to get it done anymore. My son is an avid gamer and has demonstrated to me that his business-grade laptop gets better frame rates. So, we are shopping for a better and more generous graphics card.

Another area where we will be expanding is the system RAM. The RAM is DDR4 and it’s fast, but the system comes with only 8GB. Our present plan is to double it.

No documentation? I know that the trend is to not include install/recovery media, but come on - there should be more than just a quick start in the box.

This is a decent desktop system that would be find in a business environment, but it falls a little flat when it comes to gaming. It needs a better graphics card (well, at least more video RAM) and it needs more system RAM to be a respectable gaming system.

These lightweight headphones are good for when you ar on the go. although they come without a carrying case or bag, they fold and are small enough to tuck in a bag or backpack. They charge via the included USB cable. a full charge takes about 2.5 hours but there is a 15 minute quick charge option that will extend your use by 2 hours. The mic is built in and the button controls (on/off, volume, change tracks, pause for calls and resume ) are on the ear pieces. There are LED indicators for the functions and when charging.

Comfort is okay. The band adjusts for different head sizes and does not bind. The cups are padded but the whole time I had them on I was aware of them. While they did not make my ears sweat or hurt, I couldn't say they were soft or cushiony or especially comfortable. They do not block ambient sound at all. Music quality was adequate. The base is impressive but everything else is fairly pedestrian. It does work well for making and taking calls. They do feel flimsy and one of my ear cups had to be popped back in. At the current asking price of roughly sixty dollars I expect more. They are okay for running errands around town but not comfortable enough for me to wear for an extended period. I liked the portability and lack of weight. Performance was adequate.Quality was fair to middling. all things considered they are average at best with only a superior bass and easy portability to recommend them.

I don’t love it. This seems overpriced for what you get. For the price, I was expecting it to look more like a photo frame but instead, it kinda feels like an old monitor. My goal was to hang it on the wall during art shows with process videos playing. It will work OK for that but I’m disappointed that unless the video is in the exact proportion of the frame, it will always look a little “off” and there’s no means of changing how it’s framed in the display.

I think it’s at its best without the clock or any other additions.

The pros: It really does work right out of the box. It only took minutes to get photos onto it. The big screen is nice, I can see details in my photos. It is also bright with vivid colors. I like that it is flat which is why it performs better than an average monitor as a picture frame. The simple black frame doesn’t detract from its appearance. I like that there is an app and my husband and I were able to add photos, and I also like that there is a way to add photos via card in case software changes make the app obsolete. With the app, I was able to get videos onto it in minutes. I also like that it has a large amount of storage space and the means to expand it..

The cons: It is slow. I didn’t love the way the photos are displayed. I also hate the default animations because they are a bit cheesy. I want it to fade or some other non-intrusive way to change photos, and there is no means to edit it. The features are incredibly barebones. I hate that the default includes the time etc, I just want it to look like a photo frame! The audio is a bit tinny, much more so than a television etc. I also find it bizarre in 2023 to have an item that warns that it can destroy a USB if it’s removed without turning it off first…that seems like such an old-school problem!

I wish the plug was white because the black looks bad against the wall, and I prefer a minimalist look.

For the price, I feel like this could be better. There are just so few options for customizing the display.

When my much more expensive Bluetooth on-ear headphones broke I was a bit frustrated and decided to go back to something cheaper. As expected, this product is less comfortable and clearly uses cheaper materials and construction, but I can't really complain given the price. The sound quality is fine as far as I can tell. The battery life is decent but noticeably shorter than my previous headphones. Also, the low battery warning is a very annoying loud series of beeps that repeats periodically until you charge it. So if you just want to listen for 5 more minutes or get through the last couple of minutes of that video and then charge it, well too bad, because the beeps are going to annoy the **** out of you until you charge it. Also, the pictures in the instructions were not clear to me at all, and it took me a while to find the charging port (you have to tilt one of the earphones to reveal the port which is otherwise hidden behind the headband).

Also, unlike my previous headphones, this one does not work well with my tablet's media volume sync (when the headphones are turned on they always revert to a default volume, they don't remember the last volume used), so I had to turn sync off to avoid constantly having to recalibrate the volume of the headset relative to the tablet.
It works but doesn't do well with high resolution.  Problems if going to a spilitter or switch.  Works fine from regular VGA-HDMI with audio AUX.

The overall sound is great - no complaints on sound. The biggest of all is that they dont translate well over to PC. Microphone is REALLY bad. People either cant hear me or they say i sound like im far away and in a can. Also cant get them to pair up with newer(2020/8 months old) Sony tv and has bluetooth capability. If these issues could be solved with software updates, they would simply be the best headphones I personally ever had. However my Logitech Pro X wireless(not bluetooth) headphones exceed the Bose 700 in all departments and cost over 50% less
It solved my Hactintosh audio problems and it sounds fine, not great

Let me start out by saying that I bought these mainly for streaming on my iPad. I purchased these as a replacement for a pair that I really liked that broke off in my iPad.
These came very quickly. Like ordering them at night and getting them the next morning quickly. So I immediately plugged them in.

Pros: Sound good when you are streaming video YouTube/Prime, etc. I watched several hours of Ray Donovan & a variety of YouTube videos and these were good for that. I don’t know that they block out much ambient noise or have much noise cancellation.
* Plug in/remove very easily to both my iPad Gen 5 and iPhone 8.
*Magnetic ear buds really do help keep cords from tangling.
*One year warranty
*MFI Certified

Cons: There isn’t much bass to speak off when streaming music/watching music videos. I purposely played a variety of music and on a variety of platforms hoping they would pick up the differences, but they did not. I had to really crank it up to get the even close to the sound I wanted. I did notice better sound with the music on my phone than on my iPad but that’s not where I’m going to be using these most of the time. And I still didn’t consider it great.
* I found the buttons to be clumsy. The last pair I had were flat and so much easier. I kept fumbling. I did like the options they gave, I just wish they were smoother to use.
*Ear buds are one size fits all so hopefully the size medium they send fits you. I used the small pair from the ones I was replacing and they fit/felt much better. They sounded a little better too. Didn’t notice any change in noise cancellation.
*I did not receive the silicone pouch. Mine is the burlap bag pictured like you would get at the dollar store.

I have found with the numerous reviews I’ve read that the plug in breaking like I had with my other pair is fairly common. I read it about this brand too. I honestly don’t understand why when lightning plug technology is there with charging cables, they just can’t seem to get this right...baffling.
The other brand I purchased were Geardon Lightning Connector Headphones ($26) and I like them. They broke after 4 months of regular use. I used the product support option, talked with Amazon digitally, got the vendor email & the vendor replaced them with a 3 day turn around! I’m impressed. No additional warranty was purchased. Fingers crossed. The magnetic pair is now my back up.
The sound on these headphones is great but the headband adjuster slips out of the notches to easy it will not lock in place,cord is very long also

I got this for the bath, as I often like to listen to an audiobook.  The quality is a little tinny and not as loud as I'd like, but it does work.  The back cover over the plug doesn't like to close all the way and needs to be forced a bit, but it seems to be waterproof so far.

This review is for the rock bluetooth 8" speakers. I figured the larger size speaker would provide better bass and better sound compared to the smaller 5 1/2" models, but I have not been impressed. The bass is lacking and the sound generally sounds weak - like the radio in an old car or an AM transistor radio. . . just weak, somewhat tinnie. Fortunately I got them through Amazon Warehouse (used like new) for half the price of the new ones, so I'll go ahead and use them til they die. I've gotten spoiled by the great bass and sound my little Bose Mini Soundlink puts out, so when it's time for patio/pool/landscape speakers, next time I'll probably spend the bucks on Bose.

* I should have read that it doesn’t come with a normal charger, instead it came with a micro SD charger

* I used my old skull candy charger to power up these little guys and went to use them the next day at work.

* I work 10 hour days. My right ear bud died at 5 hours in. And it kept saying “low battery” in another language.

* My left ear bud was fully charged still in the case, which I then went to use, and realized that this side spoke in English. At this point they started to hurt my ears, so I took them out.

* these are not noise cancelling, but they do have good sound quality.

*read before you buy; just because it’s inexpensive doesn’t mean it won’t come with a headache or two and I decided mine weren’t worth the headache. I need earbuds I can depend on and these were not it. I listen to music throughout the day at work and occasionally will power up my wonder-boom to give my ears a rest. I work in a closed door pharmacy, so when I need to tune things out, I can. I’ll be grabbing something else & giving this away to someone who only plans to use these for short periods of time.

*the breakdown shows the right ear maintaining a charge of 3.5hrs and the left 8.5hrs for a total of 12Hrs. It’s much shorter than the average wireless earbud, hence “DIME”

*I got the black pair. Cute & compact; just not for me. I’m incredibly picky; things have to stay in my ear (even with the smallest ear grip and these being a smaller ear bud themselves, I still struggled; so I flipped them up longways and tucked the tip into my upper ear area instead of swinging it low.

Once set up these headphones are not bad for the price. The sound quality is good. However the instructions are useless. The promised aux cable was missing though the charging cable was included. Pairing too an inordinately long time but was ultimately successful. The cushioning feels firm though comfortable. Noise cancellation is good. They charge quickly and the charge lasts.

I really love this device but unfortunately I got a bad one ( apparently it has a problem with video chip) .
The seller is very agreeable & offered to give me a Refund. It's going back but I'll be buying another.
I watch a lot of videos & read news articles and find the larger screen is much easier for me to hold onto in bed especially.
Sound is really so much better than the old models but at least with the iPad Pro I got, I experienced problems with video
Playback ( shadowing & freezing especially with YouTube and some websites. ) After talking with APPLE, it seems like it was probable that mine might have a bad video chip. So now I'm on the hunt again for a replacement.
Amazing how much lighter this is than my old iPad2.

OK, I’ll preface this by saying that while I have used Windows machines, I prefer Macs. So get that out of the way early. As for this particular laptop:
1) it felt a tad unresponsive to me, not horribly so, but noticeably so, at least in comparison to my 2-yr-old Macbook Pro. Certainly faster than my other, older laptop (5 yrs old), but still things seemed to lag a bit disappointingly
2) It’s nicely thin, you can see the dimensions and weight. It feels a bit heavy to me in terms of true portability, especially for having plastic parts
3) I wish it felt more sturdy. The top is strong, and the hinge feels nicely solid and durable. But the bottom and keyboard sections--the black plastic parts-- feel cheap. And I’m not a fan of the slightly rough texture on the trackpad. Keyboard is a nice full size. I prefer a very sensitive, speedy trackpad, so default settings were slow for me, but easy to change. I also find the glare from the black border a bit distracting at times.
4) Wi-fi and Bluetooth set up were easy and quick whether pairing devices or connecting to my network. No problems at all.
5) This isn't a review of Windows 8, so I'll leave that alone save to say I'm not a fan. If you are, this is it.
6) The touch screen is responsive and pretty accurate, though for the life of me I can't figure out who is looking for a touch screen on a laptop. Obviously, some people must like it, but I can't imagine using it hardly at all due to the horrible ergonomics of it. If you're looking for a touchscreen laptop, this seems more than sufficiently responsive and accurate.
7) screen is colorful and bright. Sound is solid--nothing to write home about, but not too tinny. It is a laptop after all. Certainly fine for streaming youtube videos and if you're not picky, movies.
8) Not sure I'm buying the battery life based on a few days of use, but I'll update as needed

It's always hard to compare cross platform. Given a choice between this brand new one and my two-year-old Mac, I wouldn't even consider switching. But then, this computer isn't really aimed at switchers I'd guess. If I can imagine just starting out neutral--probably impossible to do--I think I'd find it a mid-range product: a little noticeably slow in some respects, a tad heavy but not deal-breakingly so, some sense of durability in the aluminum and hinge but feeling a bit cheap in the other parts, decent screen and sound, very quick and easy plug-and-play-and-connect set-up, a "bonus" touchscreen that I probably wouldn't use at al.
This bluetooth headset works as expected. The sound is clear. However, there are newer versions of earphones that work as well and are more comfortable, less likely to fall.

These earbuds are small and light; very comfortable to wear. Volume is loud enough. Battery life is great. Unfortunately, sound quality is mediocre. There is decent bass, but higher frequencies are more muddy than crisp. Not very enjoyable for the music I like to listen to. Even at this budget price level, I rate these earbuds are below average because of the sound clarity.

I use this with my cell phone via Bluetooth when running, or at the gym. Inside my local gym I can get as much as 75 feet away from my phone and still keep a signal, as long as I stay in the same room. The sound is pretty good, with decent bass, although BT muddles most of the high end. They stay in the ear pretty good, and the flat cord doesn't get tangled or knotty the way a typical round cord does.
What I am not happy with is the battery life. Last week I took a fully charged set of these for a 90 minute trail run, and when I was done the battery was dead. My phone was less than a foot away from the set and I didn't do any fussing with it, just put them on and went. This happens more times than not. No sure if I can return them or not, but for sound I give them a 4, but battery life a 2. Hence, my overall 3 stars.

It was easy to set up and connect to my phone and laptop. Projector met all my needs with the exception of  producing quality sound, you can barley hear.  Picture is nice but the sound.  I wish I could hook up to firestick

Otherwise the audio and video quality is great.

The good news is it has a mounting screw adapter that fits my blue yeti microphone which I wanted to use in the first place. For the money the mount is worth it, but get your own microphone because the supplied one is very bad, I can’t stress how bad it is, don’t even try to use it.

They sound great, but I didn't like how they fit.  They felt loose around my head.  If I looked down or moved my head forward or back they would just fall off.  There was no tension in keeping them on my head.
Used for about a year, then had to get rid of it because the sound was so staticky. Not that great.

It works ok but the part that connects to the audio jack of my iPhone broke within the first day of use. Only the plastic part broke so it's still usable, but it's harder to connect to my phone. Overall, I don't think it's worth what I paid for it but it did the job, I guess.

EDIT: Leaving my original review below, but it seems it was a faulty base that gave us an extremely short working range. We were able to exchange our package and it's working now. I really regret not listening to the bad reviews.

First the good things: sound quality and ease of use are great. I love the clip so I can attach it while I'm out walking. Now the BAD: The third time I used it, a line appeared down the middle of the display and it has not gone away. I didn't drop it or anything. I just turned it on and there it was. Other than that... I really love this thing.

It works just fine and was easy to set up. As some other reviewers have commented, it does have a hiss much of the time. It's only annoying if the sound is low or no sound at all. I'll be printing a case for it once I design it (and I'll link/list the thingiverse object here if I remember).
It does provide decent power to my minimal speakers.
The jumper next to the volume is for power. I'll be wiring a rocker switch to cut power, as pulling the plug causes a jolting noise, and there's no need to leave it on all the time. The (blue) LED is pretty bright, so I'm hoping the case I make will let just enough out to be aware, but not light up the space around it. The length of the power cable is silly-short.
It's small and *light*, so if anything, making a case to keep it stabilized on something is important.
I have a 12V solar panel/battery going to my treehouse that I will likely buy another of these (without the wall wart) and power from that to drive some desktop speakers.

I wished this camera did not pushed the envelope in the 30x optical zoom. We tested this and on play back the picture was very granular and shaky. I mean really shaky. You will need a tripod to reduce the shaking effect. We compared the output with one of panasonic camera that also had a movie function and we found that was better than this HD camcorder (for about the same price).

However, the zoom button was not hyper sensitive and hence you could zoom in and out without the picture looking like you were traveling through the stargate (sorry, for the syfy fans). It was a very easy and light camera to use and the menu was not overtly complicated in that within one choice you do not have to go into many steps to get what you are looking for - in fact there are only 6 menu options and within each one there is up to 6 choices. Great ones that we found actually worked included the face chaser (useful for filming moving objects coming towards you!) and the noise reduction (reduced the wind muffles). The camera is on as soon as you open the side wing with the view - there is no longer a viewer for the eye (thank goodness).

Works great with good lighting - natural and artificial. But does not work too well with dimly lit rooms. We noticed that it really picks up the sound real well so try not to talk as you are filming as we found we ended up being more focused on that than watching the movie. The down side on this camera was that you needed to buy a memory card and a big one at that as there is no hard drive with this camcorder; what is available only allows no more than 5 minutes of movies.

The camera is okay, not great as you can get better pictures on a stand alone camera. There is flash light, which some camcorders do not have. More useful as a camcorder than a camera - so a tad expense for just a camcorder without a hard drive.

The Fire Stick works fine but the Roku has more features, like volume control.
I had low expectations, and they didn't let me down. These do not produce good sound. You get what you pretty for.

I'm very conflicted writing this review. As music listening and noise cancellation devices, they are wonderful! You can wear this in a noisy environment and get lost in your own tunes or just hear yourself think. Also, it has a similar functional design as Air Pods that allows air in to make it comfortable to wear without the vacuum "under water" seal effect that other ear buds have. So out of the box, color me impressed- comfortable and sounds great, what could be better, right?
Well, the reason I wanted to try Jabra over other brands is their commitment to call quality. Back in the early days of Bluetooth, Jabra was one of the kings if you wanted to ensure a clear 2-way conversation on a call. A lot of portable audio devices these days overlook mic quality and put all their effort into music / playback, with Apple, Sony, and some other big brands being the exception.
Sadly, these Jabras don't seem to deliver in that regard. People we call constantly complain they can't hear us, that we sound far away, under water or over-compressed / missing parts of our voice. In quiet environments it seems to work ok, but maybe the noise cancellation bit is working overtime? I don't know. All I know is I'm so disappointed with the call quality, I can't rely on these if I want the other party to hear me clearly. Yes, the ANC is awesome. Yes, the music sounds good. Yes they are comfortable. But if you need to switch to another headset to make a phone call, these are silly. I really wish it wasn't so.

Expensive. But it is nice to have a tablet In the dash of a 2007 Escalade. Haven't got the video out feature to work yet. The temp setting you see on the top of the screen doesn't work so I found it in settings and disabled it. You can send email to tech support for help and wait for replies and generic answers and sometimes go in circles. It was plug and play for my vehicle without all the expensive adapters you see in other videos you watched. SOME steering wheel controls work for. The most frustrating thing for me is the unit freezes up and you're stuck on whatever screen you were on and no way to reboot without turning off vehicle. Major pain when you're on the highway or turnpike. So wire in a separate on/off button hidden somewhere for this scenario. Sometimes it freezes and goes to black screen so you lost Waze or Google Maps. I tether to my hotspot on phone with Visible Wireless and been working for me. Another complaint is about the screen customization. Not many. You can change your default apps when you click the map icon or radio icon etc. My Android Auto did work but I don't use it. The Android Auto is made so you do not use phone while driving.  The Easy Connection does mirror my Galaxy S10 Fe 5g but with the default screen the way it is you're not going to see it any bigger than your smart phone display. I have no complaints with the sound (factory Bose in Cadillac)  You do have Eq settings and time delay options to play with. The installation instructions if you want to call it that are ridiculous. But if you ever installed a stereo you will figure it out  I do not believe this unit has dual zone feature so that's a huge bummer.  And if the video out feature doesn't work it will get exchanged.  A purchase is only as good as the tech support when needed. That's why my rating is what it is.  Can't drag and change the screens as seen on other units. The XM app is either full screen or minimized. There's limitations like that. I don't like the big band across the top and bottom and not allowing the user to adjust it more. we done need the huge buttons for the phone. Definitely nice things to like about the unit though.  Will update more as time goes on.

After using these for a couple of weeks, it became clear that I was not going to be happy with them.  I am no audiophile, but I just found the total sound lacking.  Not sure what, I tried various equalizer settings on both my computer and an echo dot.  Yes, they look great and have a very low price.  However, I eventually went back to my Bose Companion 2 powered speakers, which I have always liked.  However, I am keeping these, as I am not completely disappointed with them and may find a use for them in the future.

This works.  It's the typical run of the mill bluetooth speaker, though.  The sound quality is fair.  It isn't great and it isn't bad.  The battery seems to last a good while.  I did have some trouble pairing, initially.  But after a few tries it took off and worked fine.  I use this for travel.

I don't know what the fraction is. But when I received the item, there are some small broken pieces inside and I can hear the sound of it. I tried to make it out but it's very hard. So it has sound until now.......... BTW, the signal is good.

Overall, these are a generally OK pair of headphones. While the sound quality won't please an audiophile, it is more than acceptable for general use. I found them to be better suited for movie watching rather than music listening since the bass and upper range are rather muted. Decent quality midrange.

It scores pretty high with regard to comfort. Lightweight, easy to adjust, and nicely cushioned.

I was not impressed with the noise cancellation feature. Yes, it does cut down on some background noise when the cancellation feature is engaged (simple switch on the earpiece turns it on and off; it runs on a AAA battery). But, the sound isolation is actually less than I get with a quality pair of properly-fitted ear buds. I could easily hear ambient sounds with the headphones on.

The track skipping feature does not work with the Fire. The manufacturer does not claim it would, so no stars are detracted for that. I mention it only in case Fire owners are thinking about using that feature. Other than that, it works perfectly with the Fire - made it much more enjoyable to watch videos than using the internal speakers.

I'll give this 3 stars. It offers OK sound quality and decent comfort, but it's billed as having noise cancellation, and that feature is not well implemented.

9/1/18 - Sadly, I've had to edit my review from 5 stars to 3. The headset on its own is, of course, beautiful and has held up well with 40 hours a week of constant use, but alas I lost the audio on the left side. I can jiggle the wire and voice and sounds will flit through, or I can try to toss my head about, swishing the sound from the right to left ear, but it does make it hard to work that way. I think perhaps this was made for a leisure and not a work environment. Too bad It should be built for both.

I know these were manufactured for music but I bought these because I transcribe for a living and needed a great set of headphones where voice quality has to reign supreme. The type of transcription I do is for recordings taken in some difficult encounters and environments with some pretty darned difficult people, and I have to catch every word and every utterance. I have a great little cache of headphones and earphones at my desk. Each gives different voice quality and oftentimes I have to switch them out depending on the circumstances but none were really good. My last headset that was very good lasted about a year, but it was the 2nd one in two years, so it looked as if it were going to be an annual purchase and the reviews on it were getting shaky. I was reluctant to purchase these because they were a little more than twice the price but my less expensive options just weren't cutting it. The first thing when this arrived, is these headphones arrived in a beautiful wooden box. I mean who does that? I thought these people are serious about quality. The next thing I loved is the braided cord. No more broken and worn cords. And the part that plugs into the ear cuffs are real plugs, no more frayed and broken wires at the junction. The headphones are beautiful and I've received many compliments. They seem to work well for sound deafening (not necessarily cancelling but I work in a loud office with many background conversations going on simultaneously). I have a fat head but they fit nice, and the length of the head band is adjustable for a customizable fit. Cord is a tad short for me, but is not a deal breaker. I like the length better than the 10' one on my old set which was always getting tangled and run over by my chair. I have no opinion on how good these are for music as I'm looking for voice clarity, but for my purpose I am more than pleased. Five stars.

This is a truly wireless security camera system. The cameras operate on four CR123 batteries each, and lithium-ion batteries are included. That's a big plus, because you can install the cameras most anywhere. Setup took me a little over an hour.

It might be costly to replace lithium-ion batteries regularly, so you might consider getting rechargeable batteries.

The cameras are not pan-tilt-zoom cams. They're fixed. But the mounts are little metal domes, so you can manually aim the camera most any way you choose. The cameras have strong magnets in them to stick them firmly to the mounts. You can also stick the cameras to any steel or iron surface. You might keep in mind that since they're only held by magnets, the cams could be stolen easily if located in easy reach.

You start setup by downloading and installing the Arlo app on your device (phone, tablet, etc.) Then you create an account, agree to the terms, and follow the on-screen instructions for setup. The free version of the app supports up to six cameras.

The Netgear Arlo camera receiver/router connects to your Internet router with an Ethernet cable. It has a wall power supply with a six-foot cord. After it establishes a connection with the Internet router, you then pair the cameras, one by one, with the camera router. That takes about twenty seconds each.

This is where annoying things started. The app has motion detection on by default. Six cameras started slamming my email inbox and notification banner with motion detection alerts. It took a while to find the switch to turn motion detection off. You get to it by clicking on "mode" at the top, then the name you gave your camera system, then click on "disarm."

There's no batch delete feature in the app (not one I could find anyway) to delete all those motion detection videos at once. I had to go through and delete them one by one.

Notifications said the base unit and all the cams needed firmware updates. The update for the base unit went smoothly. The camera updates did not go so smoothly. Almost all of them said "update failed - camera rejected upgrade request." I moved the cameras close to the base unit and retried the updates, one camera at a time. Success.

These cameras do not continually take pictures, which is probably a battery saving feature. They start taking video or pictures only when motion detection is triggered, or when you manually click on "live" on each camera's thumbnail picture. The live stream takes several seconds to start. So the best setting for security would be motion detection active, but that might mean a lot of notifications. If you want to just take a look at the cameras to see what's up currently, that's kind of a problem. Each camera has to be started, and there's several seconds of wait time. (Edited to add: Adding to the wait time is that it appears video clips are not stored locally but rather uploaded to the manufacturer's site then downloaded back to your device.)

Let me put it this way: If motion detection is switched off and you hear the sound of a varmint on your porch and you want to take a quick look or grab a quick snapshot with one of these cameras, that's just not going to happen. You have to rely on motion detection being on to take the pictures for you. With motion detection off, at best you'll be able to take a look after several seconds of camera startup and buffering. (Edited to add: And if the varmint is moving quickly, you may not get a picture of it at all---just the motion detection alert and a short video that didn't capture what set the alert off.)

In contrast, I have three IP cameras that are always on. I can open the app for them and see a live picture from all three cams at once and grab a snapshot from any of them. But they all require hard-wired power, so it's a trade-off.

When you start the app, you see thumbnails from the last time you ran the live streams, or from the last motion detection. Those thumbnails can be hours old. I don't know if it would be possible, but if the Arlo app and cams had a "refresh all thumbnails" feature, that would be a big help in getting a current look at all your cameras. Then you could start live streams if you choose to.

For some reason the app will only support running five live streams out of the six cameras. You have to stop one of the streams to start the sixth.

If you install the Arlo app on more than one device, only one can be logged in and viewing cams at a time.

(Edited to add: A couple of other issues with the app: If you haven't opened the app in a while, you may get a notice that your login token has expired and you have to re-enter your password. More seconds lost if you got a motion detect alert and want to take a quick look. And sometimes you have to dismiss an ad before you can go look at the cams. And on my Kindle Fire, the Arlo app tends to go into some sort of loop sometimes, and I have to shut down and reboot the device.)

Picture quality is good. It can be set to lower resolution to maximize battery life, or medium or high resolution. The cams also have a night vision mode that can be switched off individually using the app. This is handy if you want to position the camera to look out a window at night. If the night vision mode is on, the IR led will reflect off the window at night like a bright light. Turning off night vision mode will avoid that. However, this still requires the exterior to be well lit or to have an outdoor IR source. The cameras' built in IR illumination isn't long range. It will light an average size room though.

The manufacturer says the cameras are weatherproof and can be positioned outdoors.

The web site says the cameras have a 300-foot range line-of-sight. One camera I placed about fifty feet from the router had difficulty connecting. It seems that the number of walls and other items between the camera and the router can have a big effect on connection, which isn't unusual with any wireless devices.

I think for a basic security system, IP cameras might have a few advantages over this system. But this system has its points, such as install-anywhere convenience and fairly simple setup. For actual security, keeping the system motion-detection armed and just letting the cameras grab and upload pictures and the app send notifications is the best solution, I would think. If you want to monitor live pictures yourself, or even just glance at very current pictures from time to time, I'd think this system wouldn't be a workable solution.

The Onkyo HT-S5100 Home Entertainment System sounded quite good when listening to the radio, and I really loved the self-calibration feature to set the speaker phase/power-level based upon our optimum seating position.

When the receiver is played at low to mid volume ranges, the system was impressive, but there was distoration at higher levels when the speakers were driven beyond their capabilities.

As far as a Stereo Receiver goes, I'd give it high marks, but as far as a Home Entertainment system goes... in my opinion, I'd purchase something else.

I found after many frustrating hours of trying to get the receiver to work with my other HDMI components, that all of my attempts were in vain.

I'd essentially purchased the system on the recommedation of Consumer Reports (They crowed about the HT-S5100 having the best sound of any system they'd ever tested, and it was one of the only ones offering 7.1 versus 5.1 stereo surround).

I eventually re-read the Onkyo Owners Manual and found a small blurb regarding the audio of the system not working with HDMI...

I freely admit I'd blown-off the fact that analog/digital connectors were shown on the Quick Hook-Up illustrations (thinking these were alternative connections for those unlucky soul's who didn't have HDMI), when I finally resorted to contacting Onkyo for assistance/confirmation.

They confirmed my worst-fear, their HDMI's were (Pass-Though). When asked why they even bothered to put HDMI connectors on the system, the reply was (some consumers desired them).

Personally, I feel if a system has HDMI connectors present, that is implies they're fully compliant, otherwise their presence is misleading.

What this meant was all of my new toy's (50" Plasma, Blu-ray player, and Xbox 360) could only pass on video (not the higher quality audio signals through the HDMI connectors), and that I'd have to accept a lower quality audio output due to the use of standard audio connectors.

Perhaps I'd missed this in CR's review (or it wasn't stated), as I had to purchase additional digital cabling so that I could even hear the audio content of the devices hooked into the Onkyo (added expense/wiring woe's).

If I had to do it all over again, I'd purchase the HT-S5100 as a Stereo Receiver, but I wouldn't recommend it as the hub for a Home Entertainment System to interconnect your HDMI devices.

Another pearl-of-wisdom, don't rely strictly upon the written advice of a third-party, go out and listen/view the equipment yourself, as that's what I'm wishing I'd have done!

As with anyone reading this review, I store and backup many large files - in addition I need quick access to them and this drive delivers. The primary quality I look for in this type of product is dependability and this drive has yet to let me down.

While this external drive is not as small or portable as a laptop unit - it does require its own power supply (provided) it is perfect for everyday use plugged in to my laptop. I have yet to see a USB powered 5 TB drive that I would trust.

I use it primarily to store large photo and video files once I'm finished working on them but have never had any issue pulling a file straight from there into PhotoShop, Lightroom or Illustrator working on it and resaving.

Transfer speed is really impressive for a drive of this size. That being said, I'd definitely recommend having a filing system that makes sense to you as searching through 5 TB (actually just under due to system files) for the file you need would be daunting.

I've had my current drive for quite a while, in use everyday without a single issue, so when I realized I was down to only having 340 GB available yesterday I ordered another without hesitation.

In my experience this is an awesome external hard drive that will deliver all you need it to do.
